pr_title: Switch to dynamic cert gen for tests
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/32813 and should get us out of the business of expiring test certs

Will address the more complicated cert chain in a later PR (most likely next build ops) that's already tracked via https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/39669
pr_comments:
Hey @bartonjs I finally got around to trying the snippet you suggested for us to dynamically generate certs in: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/32806#issuecomment-843574425

Everything seems mostly fine except for one case where Ubuntu is seeming to allow an expired self signed cert: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/public/_build/results?buildId=1566042&view=ms.vss-test-web.build-test-results-tab&runId=44083042&resultId=106439&paneView=debug

This seems weird as its not failing on Mac or Windows, are there any known issues with these apis on linux?

I'm also not sure if the old cert matches exactly what the new cert does, does passing in no/null eku end up creating a cert with both client/server eku? 

I guess we have always had issues on ubuntu, since there's another test that was already disabled: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/91858b0161750b7753a187d25def4704ae53cad6/src/Security/Authentication/test/CertificateTests.cs#L192

Existing selfSignedNoEkuExpired cert details:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6537861/151240592-4dad6f8a-03ec-4b13-9789-9885097db80b.png)
Azure Pipelines successfully started running 3 pipeline(s).

> I'm also not sure if the old cert matches exactly what the new cert does, does passing in no/null eku end up creating a cert with both client/server eku?

Except for specific specs that say otherwise (such as RFC 3161 trusted timestamping), a cert that has no EKU extension is treated as supporting all usages.  Since TLS doesn't have such a disclaimer, yes, a cert with no EKU extension at all is valid as both a client cert and a server cert

> Everything seems mostly fine except for one case where Ubuntu is seeming to allow an expired self signed cert: 

Weird.  We certainly have a lot of expiration related tests in X509Chain, and I can't think of anywhere that we'd have a behavior like that.

This gets us most of the way there by deleting the certs, there's still some tests skipped on ubuntu and mac, but we don't have any specific platform code that we need to worry about (and the tests are already skipped today) so this is still an improvement

issue_context.title: Update cert auth tests to generate certs dynamically instead
issue_context.body: Rather than relying on checked in certs https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/32812 which have hardcoded dates, we should generate certs at runtime to have the expected properties so we don't accidentally floor all our builds again by surprise on random dates.
comments: Also cert test is skipped due to failing on ubuntu (need to reenable)

review_comments: You mean the actual files?  I'm a bit wary about those since those are in a shared folder as opposed to when they were just in the security tests

Looks like its only Microsoft.AspNetCore.HttpOverrides.Tests which also uses some of these

```
Middleware\HttpOverrides\test\Microsoft.AspNetCore.HttpOverrides.Tests.csproj:10:    <Content Include="$(SharedSourceRoot)test\Certificates\*.cer" CopyToOutputDirectory="PreserveNewest" CopyToPublishDirectory="PreserveNewest" />
```
Actually I guess I can update those tests too and then just nuke the entire directory
Updated and moved the Certificates helper to that shared directory instead and have HttpOverrides reuse the same class which let me nuke all the cer files hopefully
